title: The merge tool posts a review record after each review round
why: Follow-up of step review-rounds-rework. Lesson 1 of 4 from lane priority-vs-merge-order (relayed 04:04 CST Nov 14, lane's own read, unchecked by triage): post the tool-printed review record right after each passing round. Triage sorts it here, not on fail-round-needs-record-before-push (coordinator's pick, 04:05): this step's title is "the merge tool posts a review record after each review round", which covers the PASS case; the FAIL-round step is a push guard for one case. Titles read, fit not proven; the coordinator may overrule. Sighting 04:17 CST Nov 14 (lane test-helper-has-a-home, tool outputs it quoted, relayed by the coordinator 04:16; unchecked by triage): once a PR head moves, `merge --review-record --head <old head>` exits 1 ("the pull request head is <new>, not the reviewed <old> ... No override lifts this refusal"), and `--fix-check <old>` exits 2 ("the reviewed head must be the Head of the newest earlier review log on this pull request ... (no earlier record exists)"). A round that passed at head A but was not recorded before the next push can get neither a record nor a fix check; the only route is a fresh round at the live head. Cost: a fresh round. Second case of lesson 1 (the first: the #3378 and #3250 lanes). Filed here, where triage sorted lesson 1 of the closed step lane-four-lessons-unfiled; the coordinator asked for it on that step, which is closed. Cases 04:21 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 04:21, relayed; unchecked by triage): the old-head record refusal has now hit four lanes: #328, #3233 (earlier), #3395 (04:12) and #3389 (local-autonomy-equals-cloud, head 93df5839b684, draft). #3389 opened its PR after round 3 and never posted a record at the reviewed head 6f367b532; six lint-fix commits later the tool refuses both the record at 6f367b532 and `--fix-check`. Route the coordinator gave: a fresh round 1 at the live head. The coordinator asks to raise this to a build step ahead of the queue: it is already doing (lane in the lane field), so triage leaves the order to the coordinator and the owner's ruling own-ready-by-priority; the case count is the evidence for the priority. Case that is new here: a lane that opens a PR after its reviews cannot get a record for the reviewed head at all. Route that worked 04:58 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 04:57, relayed; mailaudit #324): rounds 1 (haiku) and 2 (sonnet) were recorded at 7daa55fc, then main was merged in, then a fresh sonnet fix check was accepted with `--head e00b874f --fix-check 7daa55fc`. So a record posted at the reviewed head before the next push lets a later base merge carry a fix check; the refusals above hit only lanes that never posted the record. One more case where main moved under a recorded head, and the tool handled it. Data point 05:14 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 05:15, runner 10's `--reviewed` log at 05:13; not read by triage; the cost not timed): the records step on draft #3377 (merge-lint-skip-green-rollup) pushed a records-page commit, head 732293c9b3 to 8c4dfb4219ed, and so made the review record stale; #3377 now waits on a fix check at 8c4dfb4219ed, asked of lane merge-tool-audit-fixes. For #3349 the records step did not make it stale (docs-only). So for a guard or check PR the records step adds a new head, a lane lint cycle and a fix check (runner 10's wording). A data point for the records-page choice (owner item 830), not a ruling. SIGHTING 08:31 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 08:31, relayed; the coordinator read REST comments on #3401 at 08:27; the refusal text verbatim is the coordinator's; triage read none): lane silent-undo-trailer-rewrite reviewed #3401 through round 1 FAIL, round 2 PASS, fix check PASS, but posted no record row at any head, so the tool refused every row at the live head c1da982d76fb: "the --fix-check reviewed head must be the Head of the newest earlier review log; none exists". REST comments on #3401 show only lane-lint rows. Cost so far: three rounds of reviewer work lost to the record, and one fresh round 1 owed at the live head (coordinator's pick: a fresh reviewer; the tool decides what is next). Third case beside #3377 and #324's counter-case. Debt candidate (coordinator): the lane brief template says "post the record row after each round, at the head it read". Guard that would have stopped it: this step (the tool or lane lint refuses a hand-in with a review and no record row at the reviewed head). SIGHTING 09:05 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:03, the lane's account; unread by triage): #3403's round-1 FAIL record was missed before the fix push, so the tool refused the fix check. Fourth case beside #3377, #324's counter-case and #3401. EVIDENCE 09:12 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:06, from the lane; unchecked by triage): on #3401 the fresh round 1 found a real hole (code conditionals passing the negation excuse) that three earlier unrecorded rounds had missed. Evidence for the step: a round whose record is missing is lost work, and the review found a defect the earlier ones did not; not a reason to skip rounds. The owner item the coordinator names on this step: none is on the page (triage has posted none). RECORDS ON #3404 09:43 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:40, read by the coordinator): 6879572556 (head 44dcee1525e4, round 1 sonnet PASS) and 6879824600 (head 95962808606f, round 1 sonnet PASS + fix check on the merge of main, net value not owed). Round 1 ran sonnet there. The 97 min chain on #3272, #3403 and #3404 is also the cost the step's missed records add. MORE REFUSALS 11:10 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:06, relayed; triage read none of them): three more lane refusals read as "restarts the review": #3180, #2839 and #2970 (with the earlier ones, seven fold PRs: #3158, #3180, #2733, #2970, #3063, #2839, #3226; the coordinator replaced their lanes at 10:50 CST). Each lane now builds one replacement PR on the coordinator's re-brief (its own picks, undoable). REFUSAL SIGHTINGS 11:30 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:28, relayed; triage read none of them): all read "restarts the review", each routed to a replacement PR on the coordinator's pick: #3180 (now #3408), #2839, #2970 (now #3409), #3063 (now #3410), #2733, #3226 (now #3411). Classifier denials of a carried round: #3226 twice, #3411 once. REMEDY TEXT WRONG 11:44 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:41, relayed; triage read the code line and the decision line named here, in the stable clone): six lanes (#3180, #2839, #2970, #3063, #2733, #3226) posted a bare `--round 1` on a merge-of-main head and got "this record restarts the review ... A new branch with a new PR is the only way out" (merge/merge.py line 4854 in the stable clone: the text ends "A new branch with a new PR is the only way out."). The coordinator took that as true and routed five lanes to replacement PRs (#3408, #3409, #3410, #3411 built; #2733 and #2839 not built). But pr-review-record (decision, line 130 in the stable clone) has a same-PR route: after a PASS fix verifier a further fix verifier over a new head is accepted (owner item 741); a clean merge of main takes none; a conflicted merge, or any further head after a PASS fix check, takes one more fix verifier posted as the newest record's rounds plus `--fix-check <that record's head>:...:sonnet:PASS` (the coordinator says #3158's record 6881290708 shows it accepted; triage read neither). So the tool's remedy text names a new PR where the doc names a same-PR route. Cost (the coordinator's count from messages): five lanes about 30 min each, 4 extra PRs, 1 extra close (#3180 and #3226 archived by runner 10). The coordinator re-briefed the lanes at 11:41 CST to the same-PR route; #2970 and #3063 keep whichever of their two PRs owes less. The coordinator's own error: it picked replacement PRs without reading pr-review-record or `merge <pr> --reviewed`. Guard that would have stopped it (coordinator's, queued here): read `merge <pr> --reviewed` and the decision section before any replacement-PR pick. Also: #3407's `--guard no` is refused by the tool for actions/ paths (coordinator, unread by triage). CLASSIFIER DENIALS, CORRECTED 12:00 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:44 and its correction a minute later; counts are NOT measured): denied calls of `merge --review-record` in lane sessions it can name: 5 (#3226 once, #3411 once before a fresh reviewer spawn, #3407 three times, one with --guard yes). Allowed calls it can name: 11 as a floor (#3158 1, #3402 1, #3400 2, #3409 3, #3411 1 after a spawn, #3405 3 rows). The rate is unmeasured; the cause is unknown; "spawn a reviewer right before the call" is a guess from one case (#3411). Replaces the 11:28 count ("#3226 twice, #3411 once"). #3407's lane retries once; if denied again it comes to triage as an item. Home line: pr-review-record.md, "Unmeasured: whether the auto-mode classifier allows --reviewed and --review-record". DENIED FOUR TIMES 11:50 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:48, relayed; triage read none): the classifier denied `merge --review-record` in the #3407 lane (push-skip-text-says-stable) four times: --guard no, --guard yes, round 1 PASS, round 1 FAIL; the last two right after a fresh reviewer spawn in the same turn. The same form was allowed in the lanes of #3158, #3402, #3400, #3405, #3409 and #3411. The merge tool printed nothing for the denied calls, so its guard-path rule was not the cause. Without the record #3407 cannot get a lane record. The lane applies a fix commit (reverts a test file to main, q_max scoping), tries once more on the new head, and stops. Owner item 839 (pick-review-record-classifier) is on the page. Past rulings read: own-759-b and own-786-c (the owner added allow entries for other merge flags, knowing they go against his ruling that a repo changes to fit a shared tool). FIFTH DENIAL 11:58 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 11:56, relayed; triage read none): the #3407 lane's `bin/merge 3407 --review-record --head a10d57eb83efa02e48ca97e61c5a4d2ffb1806d2 --kind normal --guard yes --round 1:reviewer:haiku:PASS` was denied a fifth time, directly after a fresh reviewer's PASS (head live by REST: draft, unstable). #3407 has a clean fixed head, a reviewer PASS with no blocking findings, and no recordable row. The lane stopped and tried no other form. Item 839 now has option c as well: runner 10's own session posts it (the coordinator's third path; runner 10 has never run the command, so whether it is denied is unmeasured). LANE ACCOUNT, #3253 13:41 CST Nov 14 (lane roadmap-ref-fresh, 13:42 CST, its own words; triage read none): PR 3253 handed to runner 10 at head 3388bf6ebe, 13:42 CST Nov 14, from a lane brief at 12:42 CST Nov 13. Review took three rounds, and the record tool took one command with rounds 1 to 3 at the final head. Four refusals cost about two hours: a lone round 2, a round 1 at a head it did not read, a --fix-check with no earlier log at that head, and the 09:10 plan itself. CI cost: lane lint ran 9 times on 8 heads; 6 returned unfinished because the draft run (lane-touched-tests) had not started or finished, 1 hit a merge conflict with main, 2 were PASS before this one. Main was merged into the branch three times. Models: round 1 reviewers ran haiku (the role model); rounds 2 and 3 ran sonnet. Kin: item 835 (a replacement or carry case), lane-lint-before-push.
